subject: fennec
pitch: A fennec fox kit standing alert on a little sand dune at dusk. Enormous satin ears lined in pale peach, cream fur warming to sandy gold along its back, a fluffy tail with a smudge of black at the tip, and big dark eyes with a tiny white sparkle. Its paws are a touch oversized, like it hasn't grown into them yet, and it wears a woven leather collar with a small brass bell.
reasoning:
I'm sketching proportions for the fennec fox and kit relative to a lathed dune mound, planning dimensions so the figures' feet sit exactly at the dune's raised surface rather than at world origin.

Now I'm laying out the skeleton structure: a pelvis root joint, spine chain going into the chest, then neck and head, plus separate chains for ears, tail, and legs, building these using the chain and joint helpers with explicit coordinates for each spine point and parent/root relationships.

I'm sweeping a body mesh along the spine chain with varying radii for width and height, then setting up a countershaded paint with gold on the back and cream on the belly, possibly layered with mottling for texture.

Next I'm building the neck chain parented to the spine's last joint, then placing a head joint at its tip so the neck naturally flows into the head bone for attaching head geometry.

Now I'm detailing the skull as a scaled sphere, with the muzzle made from tapered box sweeps for upper and lower jaws, a separate jaw joint for articulation, and small sphere geometry for the nose and eyes positioned symmetrically on the face.

Designing oversized fennec-style ears as extruded teardrop outlines, positioned above the head with tapering width and sufficient height to look proportionally huge.

Simplifying the orientation for both ears to use consistent x-axis with mirrored tilt angles for symmetry. For the ear materials, I'm planning a tan-gold outer ear with satin gradient paint and a slightly smaller peach-toned inner ear offset forward, with the inner ear having greater thickness than the outer for a layered, protruding look.

I'm skipping extra details like dark-tipped fur or cream tufts for now and focusing on setting up the ear bone joint at the base for rigging. Writing ear outline coordinates...

For positioning, I'm computing the ear base location against the head's spherical surface so it sits naturally at the skull curve, tilting outward slightly. Next I'll move on to building the four legs with oversized paws.

Each leg follows a hip-to-paw chain (shoulder, elbow, paw points) with a slight bend, tapering the bone radii thinner toward the tip, and I'm placing the paws as flattened ellipsoid capsules resting just above the dune floor level.

Now I'm setting the hind legs with a digitigrade bend—hip forward, knee pulled in, hock angled back toward the toe—using four joint points (hip, knee, hock, paw) to form three bone spans per leg, mirrored for left and right.

I'm adding a haunch bulge sphere at the hip for thigh mass, then sketching the tail as a drooping chain of five points curving down and back, with a sweep radius that tapers and wobbles slightly for a fluffy look.

For color, I'm setting up a gradient from gold at the base to black at the tip using a mix function, checking which paint module's `mix` export takes precedence to make sure I'm blending colors correctly along the tail's z-position.

I also need to check the tail tip's vertical position against the dune surface — it looks like the tip's bottom edge is sinking slightly below the dune line, so I'll need to raise it.

For body coloring, I'm using countershading to blend a mottled gold-and-sandy back with a cream belly, and I'll apply a similar cream-to-gold gradient on the legs rather than a flat color. Now I'm moving on to work out the head's paint treatment.

For the head I'll use countershading again - gold on top, cream underneath, with a plain cream muzzle. Then I'm adding a collar: a small torus positioned at the neck, oriented perpendicular to the neck's tilt direction using the local z-axis to aim it correctly along the neck bone.

For texture I'll give the collar a woven-leather look using a scale-based pattern in brown tones rather than simple stripes, since that reads more like braided material. I'm placing the collar slightly toward the head side of the neck's midpoint to sit naturally against the sweep radius there.

Now I'm sizing the torus so its inner radius stays just under the neck's cross-section at that angle, adjusting R and tube thickness so the ring pokes out visibly without clipping into the geometry. Since the neck runs at a 45-degree angle, I'm treating any perpendicular cross-section as a circle for simplicity, then placing the brass bell sphere just below-front of the collar by moving along a perpendicular vector from the neck's direction.

I notice the bell position overlaps with the chest geometry, so I'm pulling the body's spine endpoint back slightly to shrink the chest and free up space, then repositioning the bell to hang just forward of the ring. I'll add a small flattened dark sphere for the bell's slit opening instead of a full torus to keep things simple.

Now I'm adding cheek tufts using small outward-pointing cones positioned on either side of the head, colored cream, plus a cream chest ruff sphere. Skipping whiskers and tear marks for now, and starting to sketch out the dune shape using a lathe profile with a rounded outline tapering from a wide base to a low peak.

Finishing the lathe outline, then applying a sandy striped texture with ripple wobble to mimic dune ridges, positioning the whole shape centered at the origin so it extends from the front tail to the back.

I'm nudging the dune's center slightly and considering a few small tan rock accents at its edge, then setting up the jaw joint parented to the head with a lowered rod shape for the lower jaw.

Still writing muzzle sweep geometry...

Still shaping head geometry...

I'll skip the eyeliner detail as too risky to place accurately on the skull surface, and instead place a small nose sphere near the muzzle tip, slightly flattened. For the paws, I'm considering adding a few small toe details to the oversized paw spheres.

Working out the front leg as a tapered sweep through three chain points with decreasing radius, checking that the paw sits correctly against the dune terrain at its position.

I'm checking paw sink depths against dune height at each foot's radial distance from center, then adjusting the dune's offset and broadening the plateau profile with gentler slope points so the feet rest naturally on the terrain.

Now I'm setting up the ear joints with proper parent-child hierarchy to the head, and defining the extrude parameters for the left ear's base position and orientation vectors.

Checking the cross product for the ear tilt directions, I realize the y-axis gets orthogonalized against x, which strips out the outward tilt I wanted — I need to pick a perpendicular x direction instead to preserve that tilt.

Computing cross products confirms both ear normals point forward correctly, giving slightly outward-back tilted fennec ears. I'm now positioning the inner ear details forward along the normal and working out the gold and secondary color values for the ears.

Writing body spine geometry...

Setting up the neck chain with "neck1," "neck2," "head" joints parented to spine3, defining roles for each chain type (spine, neck, tail, leg), and sketching out the tail fluff chain with four segments.

Now I'm placing small dodecahedron rocks scattered on the dune slope, calculating their height positions based on distance from the dune's center so they sit naturally on the terrain, then moving on to finalize the export code.
